q: What is the difference between essential and leadership indicators in BRSR?
title: BRSR essential vs leadership indicators
short: Essential indicators are mandatory for every company filing BRSR. Leadership indicators are voluntary, though SEBI asks companies to try to report them. Scope 1 and 2 emissions are essential; Scope 3 emissions, value chain impacts and life cycle assessments sit in the leadership indicators.
audience: First-time BRSR preparers and suppliers filling customer forms

p: SEBI's May 2021 circular splits reporting under each of the nine principles into essential and leadership indicators. Essential indicators must be reported; leadership indicators are voluntary, and listed entities should endeavour to report them as well.

ul: Essential: total energy and energy intensity, water, air emissions other than GHG, Scope 1 and 2 emissions and intensity, waste, environmental compliance.

Leadership: renewable and non-renewable energy split, water in stressed areas, Scope 3 emissions and intensity, business continuity plans, value chain impacts, and the share of value chain partners assessed.

sections.h: Why a supplier gets asked leadership questions
p: A customer that chooses to report Scope 3 or value chain impacts can only do it with supplier data. So a voluntary line for the listed company becomes a data request for you. Answer the parts you have records for and say which parts are estimates.

senseible: Senseible reads kWh, litres and kg from electricity bills and fuel invoices into a dated record per site, with the factor and source on every line, and prepares BRSR drafts from that data. Reports are self-declared drafts.
